tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

1	# wordstat: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `wordstat/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`).
7	- **Entry point:** `python -m wordstat ...` run from repo root.
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1** `python -m wordstat --help` exits 0.
12	- **R2** `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` reads exactly one file, decoded as UTF-8 with an optional BOM (`utf-8-sig`). stdin is never read.
13	- **R3** Counts, computed on the decoded text:
14	  - `lines` = `len(text.splitlines())`
15	  - `words` = number of matches of `[a-z0-9]+` in `text.lower()`
16	  - `chars` = `len(text)` (code points, BOM excluded)
17	- **R4** `top` lists the `N` most frequent words (same tokens as R3), ordered by count descending, then word ascending. `--top` defaults to 3. Fewer than `N` distinct words lists all of them.
18	- **R5** Default output is the text format; `--json` selects the JSON format.
19	- **R6** Output is deterministic: UTF-8, `\n` line endings, no locale use. stdout is reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`.
20	
21	## Interface contract
22	
23	### Command
24	
25	```
26	python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE
27	```
28	
29	- argparse `prog` is `wordstat`.
30	- `--top` must be an integer >= 1, else usage error.
31	
32	### Text format
33	
34	Exactly four lines, each ending in `\n`:
35	
36	```
37	lines: <lines>
38	words: <words>
39	chars: <chars>
40	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> ...
41	```
42	
43	With no words, the last line is `top:` with no trailing space.
44	
45	### JSON format
46	
47	One line: the result of `json.dumps(obj)` with default separators, followed by `\n`, where `obj` has keys in this order:
48	
49	```
50	{"lines": <int>, "words": <int>, "chars": <int>, "top": [{"word": <str>, "count": <int>}, ...]}
51	```
52	
53	### Exit codes and errors
54	
55	Errors print one line to stderr, prefix `wordstat: error: `, and leave stdout empty. `<path>` is the FILE argument exactly as given.
56	
57	| Condition | Exit | stderr (after prefix) |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| File missing, a directory, or unreadable | 3 | `<path>: cannot read file` |
60	| Not valid UTF-8 | 3 | `<path>: not valid UTF-8` |
61	| Usage error (missing FILE, unknown flag, bad `--top`) | 2 | argparse default; the last stderr line must match `^wordstat: error: ` |
62	
63	Exit 0 on success, including an empty file. Exit 1 is reserved for unexpected internal errors.
64	
65	## Example
66	
67	`sample.txt` (UTF-8, `\n` endings):
68	
69	```
70	The cat sat.
71	The cat ran!
72	A dog.
73	```
74	
75	`python -m wordstat sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout:
76	
77	```
78	lines: 3
79	words: 8
80	chars: 33
81	top: cat=2 the=2 a=1
82	```
83	
84	`python -m wordstat --json --top 2 sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout:
85	
86	```
87	{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}
88	```
89

1	"""Pure core logic for wordstat."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import json
5	import re
6	from collections import Counter
7	
8	
9	def analyze(text: str, top: int) -> dict:
10	    words = re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())
11	    ranked = sorted(Counter(words).items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:top]
12	    return {
13	        "lines": len(text.splitlines()),
14	        "words": len(words),
15	        "chars": len(text),
16	        "top": [{"word": w, "count": c} for w, c in ranked],
17	    }
18	
19	
20	def format_text(result: dict) -> str:
21	    top = "".join(" %s=%d" % (t["word"], t["count"]) for t in result["top"])
22	    return "lines: %d\nwords: %d\nchars: %d\ntop:%s\n" % (
23	        result["lines"],
24	        result["words"],
25	        result["chars"],
26	        top,
27	    )
28	
29	
30	def format_json(result: dict) -> str:
31	    return json.dumps(result) + "\n"
32

3	
4	import argparse
5	import sys
6	from pathlib import Path
7	
8	from wordstat import core
9	
10	
11	def _positive_int(value: str) -> int:
12	    try:
13	        n = int(value)
14	    except ValueError:
15	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be an integer >= 1")
16	    if n < 1:
17	        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("must be an integer >= 1")
18	    return n
19	
20	
21	def main(argv=None) -> int:
22	    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
23	        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
24	    if hasattr(sys.stderr, "reconfigure"):
25	        sys.stderr.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n", errors="backslashreplace")
26	
27	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wordstat", allow_abbrev=False)
28	    parser.add_argument("file")
29	    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
30	    parser.add_argument("--top", type=_positive_int, default=3)
31	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
32	
33	    try:
34	        try:
35	            data = Path(args.file).read_bytes()
36	        except OSError:
37	            sys.stderr.write("wordstat: error: %s: cannot read file\n" % args.file)
38	            return 3
39	        try:
40	            text = data.decode("utf-8-sig")
41	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
42	            sys.stderr.write("wordstat: error: %s: not valid UTF-8\n" % args.file)
43	            return 3
44	        result = core.analyze(text, args.top)
45	        out = core.format_json(result) if args.json else core.format_text(result)
46	    except Exception as exc:
47	        sys.stderr.write("wordstat: error: internal error: %s\n" % type(exc).__name__)
48	        return 1
49	    sys.stdout.write(out)
50	    return 0

## Contract Conformance Review

I reviewed `wordstat/core.py`, `wordstat/cli.py` and `wordstat/__main__.py` against `contract.md` and `brief.md` by reading them. I could not run anything because this session has no shell tool (only Read, Glob, Grep and WebFetch). I did not run `python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider`. I also did not run the contract examples through `python3 -m wordstat`. No files were modified.

### Required Findings (must fix; include severity)
None found in the code. The one gap is missing run evidence, covered in the first warning.

### Nonblocking Warnings (follow-ups)
- **No execution evidence from this review.** The pytest run and the two contract examples remain unconfirmed by me. The parent should confirm the test results from its own run, or rerun them in a session with a shell.
- **NUL in the path:** `Path(args.file).read_bytes()` (`cli.py:35`) raises `ValueError`, not `OSError`, when the path has an embedded NUL byte. The generic handler at `cli.py:46-48` then exits 1 with `internal error`. The contract table says an unreadable file should exit 3. Real shells cannot pass a NUL in argv, so this is very unlikely. Catching `(OSError, ValueError)` at `cli.py:36` would close it.
- **Stdout write failures:** `sys.stdout.write(out)` at `cli.py:49` is outside the `try`. A broken pipe would give a traceback. This is outside the contract.

### Suggestions (nice to have)
- `allow_abbrev=False` (`cli.py:27`) is stricter than the contract requires but harmless.
- `__main__.py` calls `sys.exit(main())` without an `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard. This is fine for `python -m`.

### Checked by reading
- **R1–R2:**
  - `--help` is handled by argparse and exits 0.
  - The file is read once as bytes and decoded as `utf-8-sig` (`cli.py:35,40`).
  - stdin is never touched.
- **R3:**
  - Words use `re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())`, lines use `len(text.splitlines())`, and chars use `len(text)` on the BOM-stripped text (`core.py:10,13-15`).
- **R4:**
  - The sort key is `(-count, word)` sliced to `top` (`core.py:11`), and the default is 3 (`cli.py:30`).
  - `--top` below 1 or non-integer raises `ArgumentTypeError`, which gives a usage error with exit 2.
- **R5–R6:**
  - Stdout is reconfigured to `utf-8` with `newline="\n"` (`cli.py:23`).
  - Nothing uses the locale.
- **Text format:**
  - The output is four lines, each ending in `\n`.
  - With no words the last line is `top:` with no trailing space, because each word is prefixed with a space (`core.py:21`).
- **JSON format:**
  - `json.dumps(result)` runs with default separators plus `\n`.
  - Key order is lines, words, chars, top, and each top entry is word then count (`core.py:12-17`).
- **Contract examples:** the sample has 3 lines, 8 words and 33 chars (13+13+7). The top-3 is `cat=2 the=2 a=1`. The JSON example with `--top 2` also matches.
